headline: Cell-resolved transcriptomic methods refine disease gene prioritisation
label: Transcriptomic Machine Learning Methods
summary: Models that explicitly handle cell-type structure and zero inflation now test causal regulators and disease genes in transcriptomic data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is transcriptomic inference that models cell-type or donor structure explicitly before ranking candidate genes or regulators. Cross-site and cross-subject differential expression is addressed by federated edgeR, which matches pooled edgeR, and by Dreamlet, which fits precision-weighted pseudobulk linear mixed models per cell cluster; crumblr extends mixed models to cell composition across lineage hierarchies. CauNagi applies causal representation learning to single-cell transcriptomics to prioritise VEXAS cascade regulators, including SPI1, NFKB1, STAT3 and FOS. A zero-inflated telegraph model couples technical zero correction with transcriptional burst kinetics. Against this, a retrospective benchmark finds active spot selection does not consistently beat random sampling, deep models predicting expression from sequence largely reflect on/off states, and tabular foundation models degrade on ancestry-dependent genetic data. The new contribution is methodological scrutiny applied alongside the tools.
